utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in the courtroom and just outside the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning Your Honours, good morning to everyone in the courtroom, this is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we continue, Mr. Russo, you referred us yesterday to map 29 and you expressed some concern that we might overlook scales. I take it that you are aware that the scale indicated on map 29, which is 1:10.000 is not the correct scale. That map has been reduced in side, therefore, 1:10.000 is not applicable anymore though what we find at the bottom is of course similarly reduced in size so that can be used to orient ourselves on this scale. Actually, one kilometre on this map is five and a half centimetres and the grids on the map are certainly helpful because the blue lines, the blue rectangles, squares, are one square kilometre. Mr. Munkelien, I would first like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony, and Mr. Kehoe, are you ready to continue the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Munkelien.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I would just like to just go back just a bit to some of the items that we talked about yesterday and you noted for us yesterday you, the UNMOs and you said yesterday at, bear with me, page 1605 -- 1604 to 1605, line 25 and then line 1 and 2 that as UNMOs were the eyes and ears of the Security Council. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So were you saying to us that the -- it was important to be accurate in the situation reports, the sitreps?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now let me talk to you a bit and I want to bring up first P67. Thank you. Can we go to -- this is a, if I may, P67 is the human rights report that we spoke about yesterday. If we could go to page 2 of that document, Mr. Monkhouse, and number 10, and this is a document that refers to a series of burnings that you observed on the 18th of August, 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we may -- if we can now go to, if I may -- am I reading the 625 ter number here -- 65 ter 4098.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just for speed of reference, Mr. Munkelien, this is a UN sitrep report for the same day, 18 August 1995. If we can go to page 2, there is a report on the bottom of page 2 -- I'm sorry, this is just the B/C/S version. And on the bottom of page 2, it notes that UNMO Team Podkonje reported. That was you folks, right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And of course this is just the military area. But let us turn our attention to the following page, the humanitarian aspects in point E. We see that at least UN patrol Sibenik in point E did report some burnings but there are no such reportings from Team Podkonje, are there?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no -- if you go back to first page, then you see why it is not reported like that because it says, "Go some like before."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're saying, sir, there.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could go back to page 1 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in the first report --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that's the report from -- highlights.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "UNMO patrols still observing looting and burning of houses." So that's the report that we reported and how Sector South reported it onwards to higher headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Stay with me, here. If we go back to page 3 of this document, of course, UN Sibenik gives us individual places where they observed houses burning but Team Podkonje does not; right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We reported it as you saw in our sitrep and then it's the Sector South headquarter who then watches the report and report what we have seen in the manner that I saw -- showed you now on page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, if we go back to page 1 just for a moment, and we look at the SMO assessment in point 2, page 1 of this document in page 2, the SMO, the senior military -- page 1, excuse me, at number 2, the SMO assessment. "The HV offensive through the SEC south into Bosnia-Herzegovina has improved the security situation in the area of Donji Lapac." So when this was written on the 18th of August there were ongoing military operations in and around the Donji Lapac area, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: According to your memory, sir, do you recall them --

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You don't recall that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us if we could move this particular 65 ter 4692 into evidence. Is that right? I'm sorry, I gave you the wrong number. 65 ter 4098.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would receive number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D92, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D92 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Let us turn our attention to yet another situation report, sir. And let me start first with, if I may -- turning your attention back to P67, and I address your attention on P67 to the entry for August the 21st, it's on item 13 on P67. Now, on item 13 on P67 it starts from the bottom of the previous page on to the top, you also include in that item some report by your team of lootings and some burnings. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And again I go back to the next situation report which is dated the 21st of August, and that is 65 ter 1237. Now, looking through this document, let's see if you can just turn to the next page which has -- page 2 of this document. It has a long report from Team Zadar, do you see the -- maybe the bottom half of that page?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And it has one, two, three, four, five, six, seven -- at least seven indications of reports of houses burning; right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's turn again to the report by Team Podkonje which is on the -- begins on the following page at entry H. If you can just flip pages, entry H that starts at the bottom and goes to the next page. If we can just go to the next page, Mr. Monkhouse. Now, in the entry for Team Podkonje, there is no entry for any burnings, is there?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that one and show me the paper that you refer to now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I refer to this --

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one that's on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The one that's on the screen is the previous -- If we can go one page back, Mr. Monkhouse. Mr. Munkelien, Mr. Munkelien. Thank you. My colleague was saying to me I keep calling Mr. Munkelien Mr. Monkhouse, and I say that's Mr. Monkhouse. Little bit of confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Refrain from any comment starting on the word M-o-n-k. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On this score, if we can go to the bottom of the page, this is the entry for Team Podkonje for the 21st of August, 1995. Now, in this reporting, this is sitrep, for instance, Team Zadar reported many instances of burnings yet Team Podkonje does not.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you just showed me first of this one was our report for that day, and then you go back to page number 1, you see the same statement as last time, "burning and looting is still going on." That was how the report went Sector South to higher headquarter. We reported to Sector South what we saw and then from then on it was not in our hands to report further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You would agree with me, sir, that in the reporting to Sector South, whatever, Team Zadar is listed as observing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, that's clear, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We've seen that. We don't have to repeat it again. Please would you put to the witness what your point is. You say there's inconsistency in reporting to and from Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear. I mean it doesn't take us 15 minutes to establish that. That's really to be seen in three minutes. What's your issue? Are you saying that the reporting from this witness is not correct or is there any comment or do you have questions about how reporting went on? Because this witness said, This is what we reported. And how they report higher up is another matter. That apparently seems to be the issue. Let's try to find out whether the witness can tell us something about that because the inconsistency is not a need to be repeated three, four, five times. Apparently, there are also the Zadar reports, perhaps are not dealt with in the same way as the Podkonje reports. I am also guessing why. Let's ask the witness whether he knows because that's what interests us, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, if I can present these documents, I'll just present it from the bar table, which is a sitrep compared to this, where, in fact, in another situation report, and I'll bring it up, the burnings by Team Podkonje were in fact reported, consistent with the humanitarian rights --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you discussed with Mr. Russo whether you could introduce them from the bar table?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I turn them over, Judge. I have not discussed that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why not be very practical in these kinds of -- the Chamber would like to hear as much information but in the most efficient way. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, the sitreps to which Mr. Kehoe is referring are part of the UNMO dossier which was given by the Prosecutor's office to the Defence. We certainly have no objection if he wishes to admit any of those across the bar table.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will take my -- that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we can focus with the witness to ask whether he can explain why because that apparently is the issue and I take it, Mr. Russo, that if Mr. Kehoe would consider that there is sometimes detail reporting higher up for some teams and for others not, then you could agree on the level of detail we find and also that the level of detail appears not to be the same for all of the teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So these are matters for which we do not need the witness, but perhaps if the witness would have any explanations as he gave, for example, that on -- what he considers his reporting to be reflected on page 1, which still does not explain why at other moments, a more detailed reporting higher up we find on other pages. So that is a puzzle which is very interesting and the Chamber would like to hear more about it, but it doesn't take us 15 minutes to establish that, the differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will be guided by Your Honour's instructions and we'll do so accordingly. On that score, Judge, I would address the Court and this will be the document, next document coming from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we note in P67, there is an entry from Team Podkonje on the 22nd of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's under number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What number in P67?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: P67, it would be A, entry 14 A for Team Podkonje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And 14 A, it notes that the team observed two houses burning. If I can address the Court to 1D13-0114. That, Your Honour, is a paper copy that we could not upload. In this particular document, if you look up in the right-hand corner at 5706, it should be at point G, the second to last page -- point H, excuse me. If we can see at the bottom of that page, it notes that "UNMO Team Podkonje reported two houses burning in the same location." This is, in fact, consistent with P67 so while the other sitreps have no inclusion of Team Podkonje reporting burnings, this one does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now you're going to ask the witness again how this could be explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I get one more. I have a lot of them Judge but I just picked a sampling of them, frankly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise, but this is document 65 ter 4794. We actually do have it uploaded and released in e-court if that would be of assistance. I'm not sure if the Court wishes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether it causes any problems if we upload it. It will be a Defence Exhibit, I take it, whether uploading from the other action would cause any problems. But at least, Mr. Registrar, if you could get it on the screen, that would certainly be helpful. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The last document again from the bar table, and I refer Your Honours to the entry in P67 for the 23rd of August, that would 15 A where Team Podkonje reports burning, and if we could pull up 65 ter 3455, which is a situation report from August 23rd, 1995. And likewise, Your Honours, beginning on page 3 of that document, we note several teams reporting burnings in the humanitarian aspects beginning at E. There was no such reporting from Team Podkonje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you want to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- ask the witness whether now on these specific sitreps, whether it's still the same explanation as we reported as we did and reporting higher up went as it went or whether he has any specific explanation for the -- well, I wouldn't say inconsistency right away, but at least a difference in detail on the reporting to Knin and then up to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you answer that question, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was waiting that you should ask me to answer it. Because from the entry of the HV troops in Knin, beginning August, Team Podkonje, Team Knin, has reported this Knin was a hot spot at that time, so they have reported Zadar suddenly came into business and then it was Zadar who got the report, we got the line in the beginning "looting, burning still in progress."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you explain, sir, why in the sample that we have, that the sitrep was -- the situation reports that was sent up did include Team Podkonje reporting burnings yet other situation reports did not? All within --

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't explain because that was higher headquarters so then you have to ask other witnesses like the one you saw, it wasn't drafted by Steinar Hjertnes, it was released by Steinar Hjertnes, it was somebody else, the OPs officer sector headquarter who drafted this one, so it was out of our hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You can't explain it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's stay, if you will, with this situation report from the 23rd --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I also see that these sitreps are prepared by Captain Anttila. Perhaps he will come up with an explanation. Let's move on. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can take a look at this situation report from the 23rd, this reports in the first page, if we can go to the first page of this. Now, you note -- it notes in the highlights in the first, second, third -- fourth highlight down in the star it says "large troop movements observed direction in and possible out of Bosnia." If we go down to number two, the SMO's assessment, "The large troop movement is assessed to be rotation of troops in Bosnia." If we can turn the page. If we can just review this and I am not going to read this, but this document reflects large amount of troop movements and HV soldiers and HV military equipment, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's all mentioning are HV headquarter and HV soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this was all going on in Sector South, was it not?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you had -- did you have any idea of the military situation at that time that the HV was, in fact, fighting the Bosnian Serbs and the Krajina Serbs in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware it was fighting going on, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that was relatively close to the areas that you had gone to, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I saw in the same report that I was arrested in Strmica that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's right. You got arrested -- if we go to page 4, you were stopped -- if you go to the last page of this document --

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was even at the highlights, so it differs what we reported and what they took in so you see it's no consistence in whatever they reported from higher headquarter to even higher headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There was no consistency?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't look like. Sometimes they reported what we saw and reported; sometimes they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, I don't know whether this is the proper time to tender these situation reports or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you've dealt with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm not finished. I have another question on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the new system as it has been discussed already, although there are no written instructions are there, that once you have finished with the witness, a document, then you tender it, it then is -- a number will be assigned and unless there's any objection then immediately we'll decide on admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go to the last page of this situation report. You were in fact stopped going back into the Strmica area, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we can bring this -- 1D13-011 -- 0110, excuse me. Now, you reported that you had been up in Donji Tiskovac, were you not?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went in that direction, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, that was in fact in Bosnia-Herzegovina, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that was a very -- according to this map, I can't see the border --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The border line is that thick black line.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, because we went -- in Strmica, you see the road into Republika BiH going, climbing up to the hill and then we went to the left and followed the border more or less. We were not crossing the border, we were towards the city of Tiskovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You note in the situation report that -- and this is on the last page, at 23 August, "UNMO was stopped on its way back from Tiskovac."

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But you're saying you didn't go into Tiskovac?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that we went all into Tiskovac. I know that we went in that direction and going in there, nobody stopped us. Coming back, they said, "Oh, it's dangerous so you shouldn't go there," then they took it into the log base according to this sitrep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But you reported in P67 that you observed, P67 being this human rights form, you observed houses burnt in Donji Tiskovac; right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, if it's in the report, I have reported and seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So that means you went in there?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, if we reported it then we went into, but we also may refer to Tiskovac as the area of Tiskovac. So maybe we didn't cross the border at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, from the report, I read under 15 A, I take it that you refer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At D. Tiskovac, not Tiskovac as such. It might be Donji Tiskovac, and I do not know whether Donji Tiskovac is what side of the border. Could you please clarify that first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There is one town, Your Honour. It is Donji Tiskovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And Donji Tiskovac is in Bosnia-Herzegovina, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you don't know whether you were in Bosnia-Herzegovina or not?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Suffice it to say in the Donji Tiskovac area, there was a lot of active fighting very close to Donji Tiskovac going on there, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that -- we didn't see any fighting when we were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, did you see troops moving in and out of the area going back up to staging areas north of Donji Tiskovac?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following the road from Strmica, we saw troops when we left Strmica and we didn't see any troops as far as we went on that road until we came back, and then we were stopped and arrested for one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And of course you were let go?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, of course. I'm here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, the area that was going on, this is during the period of time when you knew that there was fighting going on between the Serbs and the Croatian Army; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I know it was fighting in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did you know that they were fighting under the command of General Gotovina?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that any particular name on the fighters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you have any idea who was commanding those troops that were fighting up there in the middle of August --

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I will offer the 65 ter 1237, 65 ter 3455, and 65 ter 4794, as well as the map of Donji Tiskovac which is 1D13-0110.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 01237 becomes Exhibit D93. 65 ter number 03455 becomes D94. Document 1D13-0114 becomes D95. And finally, 1D13-0110 becomes D96.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections, Mr. Russo?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D93 up to and including D96 are admitted into evidence. Mr. Kehoe, if you could assist me in finding exactly -- I'm trying to find Tiskovac in such a way that I can ... First of all, Tiskovac is in what municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Your Honour, it is taking the north road out of Strmica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Strmica. And I find that, apparently, in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which municipality in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I must confess, Your Honour, that when it comes to municipalities, I'm not sure which municipality it is in. Maybe I can get some guidance from my colleagues on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that someone could help you out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Strmica is in the Knin municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the Knin municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And Tiskovac is in the Drvar municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have -- the only thing I have at this moment is map 30 in the bundle we got in the beginning from the Prosecution which is Knin municipality, apparently. I'm trying to find -- I can't find it as a matter of fact. It must be close to the border from what --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is close to the border, Your Honour. You can see from the map that we put on the -- tendered, there is a jutting out of the border a bit. I can bring that map up so you could see it. It's not a straight line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I would like to have the location in the totality so that I know what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can provide that to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you look at map 31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you go along the border, on the right-hand side you will see Tiskovac about one-quarter of the way down on the right side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have map 31 in front of me and you said go down from the top?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: From the top right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And if you go down, if you go in about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tiskovac, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see it, Your Honour? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see it. That is Tiskovac. And that is, you say, in Bosnia and I'm now comparing this with map 17 where I find in the south of the Donji Lapac municipality, just -- I see there if you follow me, I there find a Tiskovac next to Licki which apparently is located in Croatia so that's exactly why I wanted to know what I'm talking about. And then could we get the D96 again on the screen? So now I have to find Strmica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's just on the lower right-hand portion of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I try to find my way, but it seems that the border on map 17 is a bit different from the border as we find it on map 31. But first, Donji Tiskovac, Mr. Russo, you located in Bosnia as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, according to map 31 that we have in the court binder it does seem to suggest that this town is on the other side of the border into Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Therefore, I'm asking you -- I mean I can see that and has been emphasised by Mr. Kehoe. Therefore, I'm -- since I'm a bit lost comparing all these maps, I ask you whether you also take the view that this is in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, just by way of clarification, I actually have a very clear map just if Your Honour wants to take a look at it. I can just put it on the screen. I'm advised that I can put it on the screen for Your Honour's examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So we can do that just -- yes, I'm told to do it via sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. Can we zoom in so that we ... Now, the red line is the border, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Red line is the border. And then Mr. Russo, is the other Tiskovac, is that a different Tiskovac or -- in the south of Donji Lapac municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do believe it is a different one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Or is that Tiskovac Licki? Perhaps that's a different name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I believe that is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And there is also a railroad running into that valley, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Munkelien, you have observed my struggle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you help us out in any way or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there was no clear border at that time, so we went into the area, I'm not sure if we went all into Tiskovac but we were in the area. We were not stopped going in there, but we were stopped going out again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think I was at the point of tendering those exhibits. I'm not sure if they were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think D93 to D96 are admitted into evidence already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just a couple more brief topics, sir. And one of those is your statement that -- in your January 2008 statement at paragraph 44, that you noted that the Croats could have stopped the looting if they wanted to, looting and burning. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I did, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, when -- after Operation Storm, do you have any idea of the area that the military police and the civilian police had to get under control?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the area is big, but the roads are rather few, so if they put on checkpoints on crossroads, junctions and so on, they could hinder, because this looting was not done by pedestrians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And on that score, are you familiar with the NATO experience in Kosovo under similar circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I'm not sure what the relevance of that is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've been to Kosovo, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will just reread the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What was the point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The NATO experience in Kosovo is a reference to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Under similar circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Experience of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The experience of being able to control the looting and burning that had taken place when NATO came under control of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness may answer the question and we'll then see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course in Kosovo, as well, you had a lot of roads but you also had the possibility to hinder them to use the roads. It's same in the area around Knin. If you wanted people not to use the roads, you could hinder it by putting up checkpoints, like the checkpoints that didn't stop us going in, they stopped us going back. If they wanted to stop us going in, they could have done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But remember, we were UN cars and at that time, and as all missions, UN has freedom of movement, and I think that was respected going in but not going out again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was NATO successful in stopping the Serbs from looting and burning in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Mr. Kehoe, could you, before you put this question to the witness, lay a foundation on how he could have a judgement on success -- being successful in certain respects?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you say you were in Kosovo, sir?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when you were in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And are you familiar what happened in Kosovo while it was under the control of NATO with regard to the Serbs looting and burning of villages -- Albanians, excuse me, Albanians looting and burning of villages?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I toured the whole Kosovo more than most of the people in this and I know everything that happened there and I know they didn't succeed too well in preventing it, but it could have been done if they had been on the ground and if they had demanded. The one case that we were referring to now, my knowledge of Knin also stated that if they wanted, they could have put up checkpoints and prevented any looting, any traffic, unwanted traffic into any area of -- around Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, taking your answer that NATO did not succeed in preventing the Albanians from looting and burning, did they?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, that question has been answered. He said they were not successful and he said they could have been successful if they had wanted to be successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now just going back -- let's move -- what particular area came under the Croatian control at the time? Do you know the square kilometres of that area?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but it's -- the roads are still there, so I don't know the area, but what we are talking about, it's not the area itself, it's the roads leading in, and that could be controlled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the area that was under control was similar to the area that the Albanians moved into in Kosovo, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the square kilometres and I don't get your point either by doing this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Square kilometres are the same everywhere, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, no, I'm talking about that -- the area that after Operation Storm came under the control ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There's no reason to compare all these things. I mean if we are talking about being successful, possibilities, we do not compare the full detail. I think the witness said already that the UN were not successful and they could have been successful at the time so let's now focus again on this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just one correction, it was NATO, not the UN in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I noted that Your Honour said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, were you aware of the efforts by Croatian authorities to prosecute and investigate individuals who were committing crimes in the area?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just from the bar table, Your Honour, I will just by way of example, like to offer -- this is 1D13-0085, 1D13-0086.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, are you in a position already to express whether you have any objections against this tendering from the bar table. Are you going to put these to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, he says he had no knowledge so I just...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, take your time. It's clear that Mr. Kehoe wants to tender from the bar table these documents. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the last issue that we came up with was the -- you talked about the -- finding the body of Sava Babic on September the 4th of 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And were you aware of any investigation or prosecution of that matter?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I only reported it and I confirmed photos were taken the day after and from then on, I didn't follow up the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, pursuant to Your Honour's instructions, and by the way, if we could just -- I guess counsel was still waiting to see if they object to that other document so I suspect I should wait before I try to move that into evidence. I'm talking about the document I just moved from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no objection to that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is no objection against that document, then tendered from the bar table it would receive ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D97.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D97 admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a series of documents that we followed up from the -- one of our last sessions with regard to individuals prosecuted for the homicide of Sava Babic and exactly how it all transpired, it is a, in toto, a 264-or-so-page report. Heaven knows we're not attempting to -- or putting that into evidence to complete the file. However, there are a series of documents that we do have beginning with 1D13-0018.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber tries to avoid to get in lengthy documents of which only a couple of pages are dealt with. Now, as far as the investigations and proceedings against suspects or accused are concerned in relation to this woman that was killed, is there no way to agree on what, in the context of these proceedings, took place to summarise that in, well let's say, one page, to agree that this is what happens to give all the relevant information rather than to give us 264 pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do believe there is. We are not putting 264 pages in. We are just giving you the highlights of the various documents to follow up on Defence Exhibit 9, and what happened from these documents and these series of documents is that an individual is tried for the Sava Babic murder, is tried for a separate murder, convicted of both. It then goes up on appeal and the Sava Babic murder conviction is vacated and the same individual is convicted of a separate murder and sentenced. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not for Sava Babic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Not for Sava Babic but for the other murder --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- at the appellate level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Russo, is that -- does that reflect more or less -- I mean is there agreement about the very short summary and we'll see some details then I take it from Mr. Kehoe, but that is that an individual was prosecuted, was convicted for the Sava Babic murder in the first instance and that on appeal, the conviction did not stand but that he was convicted for another murder.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise, I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll try to establish together with your colleagues whether you could agree with the Defence on this course of the proceedings as summarized by Mr. Kehoe and then we'll learn about some details at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: We'll certainly do that, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And then of course we have provided all those documents to counsel and I think that it should be relatively simple to come to a consensus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just by way of guidance, Judge, on numbering, I know Your Honour doesn't want numerous numbers, and one prior witness we had introduced some documents or at least identified some documents under Defence Exhibit 9. Should we just incorporate the rest of these into Defence Exhibit 9 or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To be quite honest, Defence Exhibit 9 doesn't ring a bell immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It was some preliminary documents on the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: With the first witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we asked --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- did it have any follow-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And this was the follow-up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I have a look at that, go back to it and see how we can -- most important for me is that this seems to be investigations, proceedings, which are at least documented in such a way that I would expect the parties to be able to agree on how the course of those proceedings was at the time, and then of course the Chamber is not interested to have every detail of what witness A, B or C said during the proceedings, either on first instance or on appeal but rather on how these proceedings went. So again, whether we integrate them in D9 or keep them separate, the Chamber is more interested to see whether there is a common, shared view on how proceedings went on in relation to someone suspected of the killing of Sava Babic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can tell the Court that we have had significant discussions with the Defence and provided them with tremendous amount of in an attempt to get agreed facts with respect to the prosecutions and the circumstances of the case and we will certainly get together with them again and provide the Court is something in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then that's clear. I raise this issue - and I'm sorry, Mr. Munkelien, that we are bothering you with procedural matters - also in relation to the police log, which is also a very large document, it has been admitted into evidence, although only on two pages two small entries were used. Now it could well be that in the course of the proceedings before this Chamber that finally, you will rely on that police log again, other pages, other incidents; but if finally it does not, then the Chamber would like to discuss with the parties whether we could limit the document as admitted into evidence to the relevant pages or perhaps some additional pages for the context rather than the Chamber having to go through all of the evidence, which means all the entries in the police log and that we consider that our duty, so therefore we'd like to limit that. This already is some guidance for the parties. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The only reason I raise Exhibit 9, Judge, is the extent that you don't have documents on this same topic in various locales of -- as opposed to just putting it under one particular number which was D9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just one last question, Mr. Munkelien, and no more from me, in any event.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, you never met General Gotovina during your period of time in Sector South, did you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we called ourselves just SUNMOs, just another simple UNMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, very much, sir. I have no further questions. I appreciate your time. Thank you. I have no further questions of Mr. Munkelien.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Munkelien, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Cayley, who is counsel for Mr. Cermak. Mr. Cayley, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, I have a series of discreet topics to ask you about which I will headline for you in advance so that you can direct your mind to those topics. I also intend to refer to your statements and I'll read the relevant sections out but if you want the statements in front of you, I'll ask the Prosecution to provide them. I see you have them already. Equally, I want to refer you to some documents but to save time, I'll be referring to specific parts of documents but by all means, stop me if you want to read the whole document. And the same goes for any question that I put to you that you don't understand, please stop me and I'll repeat it to you. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will stop you and thank you for clarifying this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, the first topic is freedom of movement. So if you can direct your mind to that. Were you aware that the freedom of movement of the UNMOs in Sector South after Operation Storm was governed by an agreement between the Croatian government and the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, if D28 could be brought up in the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I ever saw this document and if I did, I think we more or less tried to say, Okay, we are white, we are unarmed and we are UN observers, so we tried the best to go forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could we have the second page of the document and I'm interested, please, in paragraph 4 and 5. Now, you'll -- I'll only read paragraph 5, Mr. Munkelien, but it states that: "UNMOs and human rights monitoring elements of UNCRO will carry out surveillance immediately in all areas except where, in the opinion of the local UNCRO military commanders after consulting Croatian army commanders, the security situation does not permit for such surveillance." So it would be fair to say that you had freedom of movement subject to the security considerations that were agreed between the UNCRO military commander in Sector South and the Croatian authorities; yes?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had the freedom of movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: But subject to security considerations?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your second phrasing of the question was different from the first one. Security considerations is not the same as an agreement between, and I think it was having consulted, isn't it? Not necessarily in agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour, we don't need to get into it but paragraphs 4 and 5 are slightly different in that respect but it's right what you're saying in terms of paragraph 5. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "It is the opinion of the UNCRO military commanders after consulting," which is not the same as agreeing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have not read 4 but ... I think 4 doesn't say anything about it. Yes. Would you also please be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, if I can refer you, please, to your statement of the 4th of September, 1999. And you say in that statement, this is D91 for the purposes of the record, and let me just find the relevant part where you refer to freedom of movement. And it's the first paragraph, Mr. Munkelien. It's the third sentence. "We were restricted in moving into some areas south from Knin but in other areas of the former Sector South, we could move freely more or less." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I want to come back to that statement in a moment, the next sentence, but in your statement that you made on the 9th and the 10th of January of 2008, and if I can refer you to paragraph 43, where you say -- do you have paragraph 43 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Where you refer to the fact that -- you speak about restriction of movement in your first statement and then you say, "This restriction was limited to certain areas at different times and the explanation given to us on one occasion was to keep us safe, as there was guerilla activity in the area. I can recall the restrictions were in place on the road to Strmica and some areas south of Knin when I first arrived, but those restrictions eased over time." That's right too, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, it is normal practice, isn't it, when military operations are taking place for restrictions in movement to be imposed on civilians and other international organisations. Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would accept that to the safety of the people, but I can also tell you that UN is normally running the flag, the white cars, and freedom of movement whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, in your first statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, could we first try to clarify where the witness says that there was restricted -- "We were restricted in moving into some areas south from Knin." I would like to know who imposed those restrictions? Was that the UNCRO authorities or were these restrictions imposed by any other authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was imposed by any other authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So not in line with the agreement as where we just saw that freedom of movement can be limited after consultation by the -- with the Croatian authorities by UNCRO. So this was not in line with the text of that agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could I take you back to your first statement, and the first paragraph. And this is one, two, three, four, five, six lines down. Do you see that? "But when it was restricted ..." do you see that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: "But even when it was restricted, we managed to find other roads and to reach the areas he we wished to visit. This happened in particular in the middle of September or in the end of September when we infiltrated into Bosnia in order to make an assessment of the area from which the Operation Storm had been launched. That was one of the Croatian positions from which Knin had been shelled."

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now the question for you is this: Am I right in thinking that what you mean here is that even when you were stopped at a checkpoint by the Croatian authorities that you would actually find another road to get to the destination where you originally intended to go?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And that would be the case even where those particular security measures that had been put in place, in other words, the fact that you had been stopped had actually been agreed between UNCRO and the Croatian authorities?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I don't believe that that fairly characterises the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm just simply developing the point, Your Honour. I'm actually asking the question, was that so even when the security measures had been agreed between the two parties? It's not clear from his statement. It's not clear from the statement he's given that he's saying that we did this when the security measure had not been agreed so I'm asking: Could this have happened even when it had been agreed between the UNCRO military commander and the Croatian authorities that they be stopped at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's very hypothetical, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: But Mr. Munkelien may know or he may not know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I clarify this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've heard the question. If you think you can say something useful to it, then please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you referred to in this, we made in one occasion another road out and that was made by the order of sector headquarter, so that means Sector South headquarter. So I mean if there had been any negotiations and any agreement, then sector headquarter wouldn't have given us the permission to go a little bit south of Strmica, go the road up and over the mountains and into Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So on this occasion, you were actually ordered to go around the security --

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: -- measures that were in place?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were limited access to the Strmica road that you saw on the map that was climbing up in the bends, there, it was excellent to control us but then we went a little bit to the south and managed to come into Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Who ordered you to go around that security --

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Sector South headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Who in Sector South headquarters?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose all the orders [Realtime transcript read in error "others"] came to our team leader via the senior military observer.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we can now move on to another subject matter which I want to address, Your Honour, and again I'll give you the heading so you can direct your mind to it. The looting and the burning, and my learned friend, Mr. Kehoe, has already asked you a number of questions --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I make a point of 11, 10, 11, 55, I suppose all the others, it should be "orders."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: He's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's page --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It's page 33, lines 12 and 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 33, I have to back to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. 34, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 34, line ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It's page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, orders, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It is page 33, it is page 33.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My -- moving my left screen is 34, but I'll check on the other one. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, you said in your second statement, and you can refer to it if you wish, that you saw looting conducted by both uniformed Croatian soldiers and by civilians; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I saw it in -- personnel in uniform and personnel in civilians clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And I think you mentioned in your first statement that you made which is D91 that on one occasion you saw three persons in uniform setting fire to three houses; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: But then in the statement that you made in 2008, you actually changed that account, didn't you? Do you recall? I'm not trying to catch you out here, Mr. Munkelien. If you go to your next statement, it's -- you'll find -- it's at paragraph 39 of the statement that you made in 2008.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the statement is more or less the same. It was three men that I visited across the field from our office.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: But you didn't actually see them set fire to the house, did you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Like I think I've stated, I say them go into the house and it was burning when they came out again so --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, you say in your first statement that you believed that the Croatian authorities could have stopped the looting if they wanted to. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, in the second statement, you also say, and you've said this already, but I'll come on to a different point, I'm not going to go through this all over again. You made the point that because of the checkpoints and the number of military and police in the area, you believe that the looting and the burning could have been stopped; yes?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do think that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, just to speak -- you're a professional army officer, you've been -- up until your retirement, you were in the service for about 30 years, I think. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, even 10 more.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: 40 years.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, the kinds of steps that should have been taken in your view which would have stopped the looting, that's what I'm interested in, and if I can put them to you and you can either agree or disagree with me. Do you think that there should have been orders from the Ministry of the Interior to the local police to stop looting and burning?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, if the police was functioning at that time. Otherwise it was the land owner, that means civilian authorities or military authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And do you think that there should have been orders to actually investigate the crimes that were being committed on the ground; yes?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but if you first prevent crimes from being made, then it's better. That means put up checkpoints and control the traffic into the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: But if crimes have been committed --

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then you should investigate them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You should investigate; yes? And perhaps orders to have combined checkpoints of civilian and military police; yes?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Perhaps also orders for mobile patrols of military and civilian police so not just static checkpoints but mobile patrols moving around the area. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Obviously, orders from the Ministry of the Interior to the police in the Knin area to actually report back to the Ministry of the Interior on what they're doing in the area and their cooperation with the military police; yes?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, reports on how they did it and the success and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And finally, orders from the Ministry of the Interior to the police on the ground to report back on the progress of investigation and the identification of perpetrators; yes?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's -- I already -- but you are talking mostly of the police, the land owner on this time I think since the civilian community was not functioning well, it was the military who should put this into practice to control the areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: But you're aware that police stations had only very recently opened in the region, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That's why I'm talking about the military. The military was the land owner at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What -- at the time, what research did you conduct in the area to actually see what the police were doing? Did you actually speak to the police at all to ask them what their instructions were?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that we were speaking specifically to any police officer, but definitely, we were around the area from early morning until dark and we saw a lot of non-functioning controls on the roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could please have D49.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cayley. Meanwhile, I would like to seek one clarification. You were speaking about a land owner which appears to me not to be an ambiguous term. I understood it, but please correct me when I wrongly understood it that you are talking about forces that exercised factual control in the area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Munkelien, you're a military man. In order to have effective checkpoints, you need well-trained personnel, don't you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And you need well-trained personnel with reasonable equipment, don't you?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And you need good intelligence on what is actually taking place in the region, don't you, to make checkpoints work effectively?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And you need communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And you also need -- the more checkpoints you have in an area, the more effective your control is, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, if it's -- if it's done properly, yes, that should help.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And those checkpoints need to be properly supervised, don't they, by a higher authority?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And that is really how you control terrain in a military or a police sense; yes?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, I want to show you very briefly this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise, I'm sorry to interrupt. Looking at the transcript, at page 38, about line 14 when Your Honour was asking a question, it indicates that you were talking about forces that exercised factual control in the area. I believe the Court's question was actual control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Factual --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I think I said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Factual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that was understood by you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, factual was the word that I understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It means --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: De facto.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, de facto control was what I'm talking about, and I have to ask native speakers to what extent that differs from actual control.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll ask my people, but if there's any native speaker to explain to me exactly what the difference would have been, then I can choose my words perhaps more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think not being a Webster's dictionary guide but it's basically the same understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, what you have in front of you is an order from the Deputy Minister of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia, I'm aware that you won't have seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Whose name was or whose name is Josko Moric and this is an instruction that he sent on the 18th of August a number of police administrations including Zadar, Knin which covered the area in which you were operating; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn the page, please. Do you see here the order is acknowledging, and I'll read it for you, it's the first paragraph: "Written and oral reports by police stations and police administration show there are daily cases of torching of houses and illegal taking away of people's moveable property in areas liberated in Operation Storm. "Most of these acts are perpetrated by individuals wearing Croatian Army uniforms. The facts indicate that these individuals are formally and actually members of the Croatian Army but amongst them, there are also individuals who are not members of the Croatian Army but are wrongfully wearing Croatian Army uniforms." Now, over the page and I'm not going to read all of this out, but what you say see in front of you are instructions from the Assistant Minister of the Interior to all police stations noted on the front of the instruction including to Zadar, Knin?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, you see the first instruction is for local police chiefs to meet with commanders of military police battalions; yes?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And the next one is an instruction to start immediately investigating individuals who had been torching houses but effectively not investigating anything -- I'll read it, it's the clearest way, it gives the most precision: "The meeting must be informed of the decision that cases of torching of houses and illegal taking away of people's moveable property that have hitherto occurred will not be operatively investigated, but a stop must be put to cases of this type as of today." You'll then see in paragraph 3 that it requests setting up of mixed checkpoints and mixed patrols of civilian and military police, and in paragraph 4 it requests that there be on-site investigation of all cases of torching of houses and looting, illegal taking away of moveable property. Now, obviously taking into account your observations on the ground of, you know, whether or not this was effective, but if the contents of this document are true, it does demonstrate that individuals within the Ministry of Interior were actually trying to do something about what was taking place on the ground at the time, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I totally agree. The intent of in this document is very good, but then there is the discrepance between the intent and the actual doing on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, the Croatian police at that time within the Knin region, are you aware of how long they had actually been operational within Knin?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could have, please, D40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could please move to the second page of D40.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, again, Mr. Munkelien, I know you've not seen this document before, but you will see that the first police station to open in the region was on the 5th of August, which was Drnis. I won't go through all of them, the last one in Donji Srb opening on the 9th of August, 1995. So by the time you arrived in the region, the police stations had only been opened for about a week, hadn't they?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And you would accept that logically and fairly, it does take a reasonable period of time after liberation of territory for a police station to become effective within a region? It takes more than a week, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It takes more than a week, but then you should have the overlapping with the military police or any that the commander, the de facto land owner had forces to put in to control this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: How, in your view, from what you could see on the ground, how well equipped from the Croatian police at this time? How well equipped, the Croatian police, how well-equipped were they during this time?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they had side-arms and uniforms and some cars. It was accurate to what the police officer should normally have.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: But in terms of vehicles available to them, they didn't actually have that many vehicles, did they, in the early days in Knin?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that, because we saw the vehicles, but I don't know in what amount.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, you said in your second statement, and I can direct you to it, it's paragraph 30, that on every occasion that you saw a burning house, you did not see any fire brigade vehicle or witness any attempts to put out the fire. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that and I agree with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, if, please, D57 could be brought up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, this next document, Mr. Munkelien, is a document actually that the learned President was referring to earlier was the daily log of incidents in the police administration of Knin district.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, is this the document that you were referring to earlier that we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's more than 100 pages yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'm actually going to be referring to a number of pages that we haven't already referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps -- yes, that's what I was alluding to, as a matter of fact, that it might be that we would use it for other --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- occasions and then at the end perhaps limit the number of pages which appear to be relevant. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could go, please, to page 18 of this document in the English version. And if you could please bring up for me the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, it's very small -- can you read it, Mr. Munkelien? Sorry, it's very, very tiny writing.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read column -- yes, now I can read all the columns.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Okay. Perfect. Now, you see here that on the 14th of August of 1995, the day that you arrived in Knin, there is a report of a fire at the UNCRO warehouse; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And you see in the next column that a fire fighting team has been sent, fire was localised and the incident was also attended, I think, by the police and a member of the military police and the army assisted in putting out the fire.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you wish, we can pause at this point because I have a number of these to show him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break and we'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Munkelien, if we could go back to the log book in front of you.

utterances.speaker: TOR MUNKELIEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
