Now, since the witness couldn't tell us anything about it, I take it that you want the Chamber to consider these entries in this police log in relation to the testimony of the witness that he didn't ever see any fire brigades or efforts to extinguish fires. And then you put that to the witness and just to avoid whatever confusion, if you put it to the witness in the way you do it, you should not expect the Chamber to take that as guidance for how to read these entries. If I could just take you to one of them. That's the 131 entry, 20th of August. That was the one where I had a question about 1225 or 2225 if you look in the original handwriting, then you'll see that it's not entirely clear but it's most logical that it will be 2225. Now, what you do is you put to the witness that this is an example as activity undertaken at a fire. Most important, perhaps, is what you do not do and what of course the Chamber will be able to read. You said to the witness, "You will see there a report on a fire, 2025 hours, B. Meglic from Grad police car, reported that a house was fire. You will see in the next column that at 2235 hours, firefighters informed that they localised the fire at 0010 hours." I have now read literally the transcript. I don't want to hide from you what I see when I read this report so that it would not come as a surprise if your reading and my reading is perhaps not exactly the same. How you could also read it is as follows: First of all, if you say that at 2235 the firefighters informed that they had localised the fire at 0010 hours, that comes as a surprise any how, that you already know at 2235 what will happen on 0010 and of course it's not what is stated there. It reads, "At 2235 hours, firefighters informed and they localised the fire at 0010 hours." Yes, that's different. We agree on that, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then, of course, what I also see there, that at least you could read it that way, that the report came in at let's just assume 2225, that there was an on-site investigation apparently only the next morning. That's also a way of reading this, because the on-site investigation was conducted between 8.30 and 1000 hours. You could also ask yourself -- no, I take that back. What I want to say, you could also look, for example, at specific aspects of this house which was near to a hospital where we saw also earlier that a fire was mentioned which was near to an UNCRO facility. I just want you to know that if you introduce this in a certain way and present it in a certain way, and if other elements or aspects are not mentioned, that of course there is a risk that there is some difference in reading of it. Now, I do understand that you want to present matters to a witness in a certain way. Nevertheless, I would appreciate if you would do it as completely as possible so that there are no grey areas where we start all interpreting the document in a different way, you not being aware, perhaps, how we might read it unless you say, I take that risk, I will pay no attention to matters that are less favourable to my case, and I take the risk that the Judges will look at it in their way in full neutrality, but not excluding matters that might not be primarily in the interest of your case. This is just an example. Mr. Russo, I could just add to that if you could not pay attention to the word "area" where a plane is used and of course taking it more or less for granted that extinguishing a fire in the woods would be the same as extinguishing a house, to be quite honest, but this is general experience, I've never seen in my life one single house on fire where they tried to extinguish that fire by a plane. I do know that if there is an area or if -- especially if it's a wooden area, even if there are houses in there that you would use planes. So therefore, you put something to the witness as Mr. Cayley did, but what you actually are doing, you're drawing the attention of the Chamber, because this witness doesn't know anything about this plane, you're drawing the attention implicitly, the attention of the Chamber to certain elements, and since of course this is not evidence elicited from a witness, you should be aware and you take the risk that we interpret this material in a totally different way, at least that there is a risk that we will do that. And I think it would be -- it's good that you are aware that using this procedural technique may result in quite a lot of difference of view and that's because documents are used during the testimony of a witness for which the witness can't say anything and they just are in evidence then and then of course the Chamber is more or less left to its own interpretation unless you specifically address certain matters. I will not lecture any further. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could I make -- thank you, Your Honour. I mean I would make a point to a degree we're all victims of our own training, our background, where we were trained, the way we practice law. I didn't in any way intend to mislead the witness, and I want to emphasise that to you now, by putting those reports to him. He had made an assertion in his statement that he was not aware at any time, at least to his knowledge, that fires had ever been put out. The only material that I had, that I could put to him to contradict him, is this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And I didn't -- and obviously the detail of it, I mean I could have gone through every single sentence and asked him to comment, but he wouldn't have been able to comment on that because he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: But the intention was to demonstrate that in fact there were attempts made by individuals to put fires out. That was all that I intended by using this documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, it's a message to the Chamber rather than to the witness. Of course the witness is not expected to know anything about these things and you could have known that from the first answer. Of course you could go through it or ask him: Are you aware of any occasion during this period? And if he says no, then it's not -- but then you of course can draw the attention of the Chamber to police logs which at least give additional information on the issue you have raised, but then of course what the Chamber most likely would like to know is for 30 days, these 30 days, how many of the similar reports are there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I mean I could -- I mean I can do that. I could have done that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You could even agree to say it's important for the Defence to demonstrate that there was activity when a fire was reported, then you sit together with Mr. Russo and you say entry this one, this one, this one, this one, and then of course you are also considering whether these were fires at UNCRO facilities or near UNCRO facilities or near to hospitals or whether these were just average houses, whether it was just Knin or also outside of Knin and then you can agree on what is there without going with the witness through all of this. And then of course we would also know whether this is, as you said just a few examples, it's the totality of what was reported in this log. Try to find ways, and I'm addressing both parties, try to find ways to give as complete information to the Chamber which allows us to see to what extent the witness who says, I never observed it, to what extent there is material to contradicts that, because that's of course what the Chamber is interested to know how reliable is the information we receive through the witness, how credible is it, and if there is any documentary evidence that could assist us in better evaluating that, then you are invited to present it to us in the most direct way. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, thank you. I appreciate the Court's direction with respect to that issue. I would just like to balance that against the Court's concern expressed earlier about essentially making a document dump on the Court. If I understand the Court correctly and allow me to propose a situation if, for example, we can agree between ourselves and the Defence with respect to documentation with which the witness cannot personally testify but which may enlighten the circumstances of their testimony, present that to the Court either before or after the witness takes the stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, if you agree on that, preferably after the witness takes the stand because we should be as blank to start hearing the testimony, although we have read the statements of the witness so to that extent we are not entirely blank. We'll have a break and we'll resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's unnecessary to ask whether you are ready to call your next witness because the witness is already in the courtroom. Good morning -- we have no protective measures, Mr. Tieger. Therefore, good morning to you, Mr. Dreyer. Before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make the solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text will now be handed to you by the usher. Will you please stand and may I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly swear that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dreyer, please be seated. Mr. Tieger, before you can proceed, the Chamber will have still have to deliver a decision on adding six documents to your 65 ter exhibit list. The Chamber therefor -- Mr. Dreyer, we have to deal with it as a procedural matter first. The Chamber will deliver its decision on adding six documents related to Witness Andries Dreyer to the Prosecution's Rule 65 ter list. On March the 20th of this year, the Prosecution requested to add six documents related to Andries Dreyer to its Rule 65 ter list. These documents are drawings of the witness on a map of Knin indicating the routes he took on the 4th of August, 1995, in and around Knin. On the 3rd of April, the Cermak Defence indicated that it did not object to adding these six documents to the exhibit list and the Gotovina and Markac Defence did not respond to the Prosecution's motion. Considering the nature of the documents and that they are disclosed, the Defence teams on the 29th of February as well that the Defence did not object to the Prosecution's request, the Chamber decides that the six documents be added to the Prosecution's Rule 65 ter list, and this concludes the decision of the Chamber. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Dreyer.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's begin simply by having you state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: My name is Andries Dreyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And what is your current occupation, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: My current occupation is I'm on a sabbatical from the United Nations to finish my master's degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You previously served with the South African Defence force and in 1995, you served as the United Nations security coordinator for Sector South in Knin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You've previously provided three statements to the Office of the Prosecutor, the first on 8 November 1995, the second on the 4th of February, 1996, and the third on the 22nd of February, 2008. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that third statement in February of this year encompassed the information provided in the previous statement, provided some attachments, and also provided any clarifying or additional information as necessary; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have 65 ter 04797 brought up and marked for identification, please. And would it be possible to provide the witness with a hard copy of his 92 ter statement and the attached appendices for reference during the course of his examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that there are objections against that so ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dreyer, you have both the hard copy in front of you and an electronic version on the screen in front of you. So let me ask you then if that document is your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of February 22nd, 2008.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity recently to review that statement?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, let me provide you with an opportunity to clarify at least one aspect of that. And if I could direct your attention quickly to paragraph 13, that paragraph begins with the time at which you embarked on the second attempt, meaning the trips into Knin. Let me ask you, Mr. Dreyer, if that paragraph in the February 2008 statement encompasses information that was provided in your first statement to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And did the information in your first statement refer exclusively to the second trip you took into Knin on August 4th, 1995 or was that a summary of your experiences during the day generally while outside the compound? And if needed, I can provide you with a copy of your first statement.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Excuse me, can you repeat, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sure. This paragraph we're looking at now in the February 2008 statement --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- in which the trips are broken down into first, second, third, fourth and fifth trip?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There's information provided here which you indicated -- information provided at paragraph 13 which as you indicated was also provided in your first statement.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I just wanted to know if the information provided in your first statement and contained here refers exclusively to the second trip you took into Knin or referred more generally to your experiences during the course of the day. For example, in particular, the last sentence of the paragraph at paragraph 13 states, "When back at the camp, we were informed that the attack will recommence the next morning at 0500 hours."

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you advised or informed that another shelling attack was anticipated on the morning of the 5th at the end of your second trip into Knin on August 4th or at the end of the day?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: At the end of the day. I'm sorry, now I understand. No, at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would be grateful if you would make a second's pause between each question and answer and slow down a little, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Everyone received that message.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: With that clarification, does the February 2008 statement accurately reflect your declaration to the Office of the Prosecutor and is the information in that statement true and correct, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if examined in court here today, would your answers regarding these matters be the same?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this exhibit at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P72.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have an objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I did, in fact, discuss this with my colleague, Mr. Tieger, and my objection is to paragraph 22 of this where it's a broad-reaching document where the witness says in paragraph 22 travelling during the day that he saw tens of people being killed, if you look at the last sentence, "I can't he be precise as to the number of dead that I saw. It was at least tens of people." I attempted to interview this witness on -- and I don't want to overstate this but on numerous occasions and was unable to do so to get behind this statement, and I have been unable to get behind this statement because there is no factual detail with regard to this other than this broad-reaching allegation concerning tens of dead. So given that particular lack of specificity and certainly our inability to get any clarification from the witness, I would object to this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, still in court where we could put questions to the witness in this respect. Is this a matter of admissibility or a matter of weight or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think certainly under the 92 ter circumstances, it's a matter of admissibility, because we are talking about a document that the Chamber is going to consider in conjunction with the witness and under those circumstances, not having the ability to flesh out particular facts so we can see what the circumstances are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently the criterion that you are using is because we are talking about the document that the Chamber is going to consider in conjunction with the witness. Now, let's just assume for argument's sake that the witness put a question, said, I've seen tens of people being killed and could not give any further information about that, would that make his evidence on that portion inadmissible?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, your -- would it make it inadmissible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It could be, of course, because without some lack of specificity it's completely unreliable and it could be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, no or little weight to be given to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think that when someone goes into this particular allegation where we are talking about homicides, I think it could be given no weight. My point in this is on this particular issue and I will give an example, one of the examples is the evidence that we discussed earlier this week about the incident that took place outside the UNMO camp. We were able to get this particular incident, investigate the incident and bring evidence before the Chamber that allowed to neutralise or have the full picture known. It's impossible with this type of statement to do that, certainly with the witness here in chambers. Now, that was why I endeavored with my colleagues over time to try to talk to Mr. Dreyer so I wouldn't be in this situation now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Nevertheless, the Chamber invites the Prosecution to seek further details in relation to paragraph 22 in the examination in chief because this paragraph, as some of the others, is not giving a lot of details and if, on the basis of these informations, Mr. Kehoe, you would need further time to further investigate, then you may apply for further time or even recalling the witness if need be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then when I said that the objection was denied, that of course included the admission into evidence of the 92 ter statement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, a few moments ago, I mentioned the annexes to the 2008 statement and also made reference to the five trips referred to in that document that you made into Knin on the 4th of August. If we could turn next to 65 ter 4799 and have that marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger, the new system is that you first call it on the screen, that you then put the questions to the witness, and that then in one breath, you ask -- you tender it, that a number will be assigned, and we'll decide on admission. So therefore, please proceed at this moment. I take it that the map is now -- the aerial photograph of the markings is now on the screen. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, looking at 65 ter 04799, a document which is marked at the top first trip and at the bottom, annex AD-2, does that reflect the route that you took on your first trip outside the compound to rescue UN personnel at approximately 4.35 in the morning to approximately 5.20 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would -- well, if I may go through the annexes and then ask -- is it more efficient to ask for numbers at the end of going through the annexes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we next then call up 65 ter 04800.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, looking at this document, does it accurately reflect the route that you took on the morning of August 4th into Knin from approximately 0600 to approximately 0830?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that was the second trip you took out of the compound to rescue UN personnel?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just going to object to the term "rescue." I don't think there's been any foundation for the need, that they need to be rescued.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think I'm just referring to the 92 ter statement but I can ask for clarification for that if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the 92 ter statement uses the word "rescued ," and I have to check whether it does, then the objection was ill-placed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May we next call up 65 ter 4801.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Mr. Dreyer, looking at the document now on the screen, 65 ter 4801, does this accurately reflect the route you took on your third trip outside the compound into Knin from approximately 0830 to approximately 1200?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: 65 ter 4802, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And looking at 65 ter 4802, Mr. Dreyer, does this document and the markings on the document accurately reflect the route that you took on your fourth trip outside the compound from approximately 1230 to approximately 1500?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And 65 ter 4803, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Dreyer, looking at 65 ter 4803, does this aerial photo and the markings on it accurately depict your fifth trip outside the compound into Knin to retrieve UN personnel sometime after 1500 hours on August 4th?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps at this time, it would be efficient to move for appropriate numbers and admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before assigning numbers, are there any objections against admission into evidence of these marked maps?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not hear of any other objections. Therefore, Mr. Registrar, would you please assign numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours. 65 ter number 4799 becomes Exhibit P73. 65 ter number 4800 becomes Exhibit P74. 65 ter number 4801 becomes Exhibit P75. 65 ter number 4802 becomes Exhibit P76 and exhibit -- I'm sorry, 65 ter number 4803 becomes Exhibit P77.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Exhibits P73 up to and including P77 are admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could next call up 65 ter 4798, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dreyer, along with your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in February of 2008 and the appendices we've just seen, did you also provide a document, this document, in which you marked, among other things, the areas in which you observed or experienced shelling during your travels outside of the compound on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you about -- I see there are other markings, I will be asking you about those as well. First of all, I want to direct your attention, however, to the three encircled areas at the far right-hand part of the document, and those would be the circle in the bottom right-hand corner, the oblong encircled area with the marking AA next to it, and the larger semi-circle with the six encircled areas within it -- four, excuse me, encircled areas within it. Do those areas represent areas in which you personally experienced or observed shelling on August 4th, 1995, and if not, what do they represent?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: They do not. They represent areas where I either heard incoming shelling, I either observed smoke rising from the various areas, or I heard from various people within the compound, including the military, that those are areas that might have been shelled, but I did not observe it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And directing your attention to the slightly squarish circle adjacent to the UN compound and to the left of the circle at the bottom right of the page and as the cursor moving, it's almost like -- there you go, right there where the cursor is. You refer in paragraph 19 of your statement to an incident where a mortar round killed people outside the UN compound after corrections of fire to get on target. Is that the area where that incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Apart from those areas, Mr. Dreyer, do the encircled areas depicted on 65 ter 4798 represent areas where you personally experienced or observed shelling during your travels outside the compound on August 4th?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: They do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I may quickly run through some of the markings, that is the alphabetical markings on this document. Can I have you look at first -- and we'll go in alphabetical order, A, which is shown towards the left side of the exhibit. What does that represent?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: I'm just trying to go through my statement, but that represents a military barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And I'll go through this quickly since it is in your statement. Is it correct that marking B which is to the right is identified in your statement as the southern barracks?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could look at marking C, which -- the registrar is way ahead of me and doing very well. Is it correct that that is a mortar section you observed by the school?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Marking D, which is -- is it correct that that was an APC that you observed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could you go to the bottom of the page, marking E. Is it correct that that apparently is at a location which is off of the area of the map, was an RSK checkpoint that you observed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Not that I observed. That someone in the compound observed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And F. Is it correct that that was an overturned Milijcia vehicle with one dead person inside?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that something you observed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: I observed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: G, is that where you were during your first trip outside the compound when the shelling commenced?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And H, which is in the middle of an encircled area, is that an area where many UN personnel lived?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, and finally, perhaps there is one more marking and if we turn to the far right, I already mentioned the belong encircled area with the marking AA next to it, what does that represent?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: That represents an anti-aircraft position that was on top of the hill which I never observed, but we were told so by the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: An anti-aircraft position maintained by what forces?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: By the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I get an exhibit number and tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Will there be any objections against this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't hear of any other objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit P78.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P78 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, apart from the mortar section marked at C, the APC at D, the checkpoint at E which I know you didn't personally observe but heard about, and the overturned Milijcia vehicle at F, did you observe any ARSK military activity on the 4th of August, 1995, during the course of your travels through the town or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: On that specific day, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that G represented the -- your location at the time when the shelling commenced. Can you indicate to the Court or describe to the Court the nature or intensity of that shelling, precisely where you found yourself and what you did when that happened?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: I can. As far as I can recollect, at that specific point at 5.00 in the morning, we were driving with two soft-skin buses trying to collect staff members from the various areas in Knin. Obviously I was responsible for the safety and security of all the UN staff in Knin at the time, and at 5.00 we managed to collect only a few UN staff members. And at exactly 5.00, I was at position G as indicated on the map. The only way I can describe it was that there was almost an immediate explosion of everything around us. It was -- there was glass flying around, there was dust. There was pieces of trees flying around. There was brick flying around. There was a ball of fire that came between me and the vehicle in front of me. I was in radio contact with the person in front of me. I directed him to get out of the area as fast as possible. We made our way across the bridge and into a residential area where we felt the shelling would not be as intense. We were not correct. It was not as intense, but it was till still there. We then made our way back down to the main road. There is only one road that leads across the bridge to the UN compound and it took us the best part of about 20 minutes to get out of there to get back to the UN compound but the only way I can explain it, there was -- it was omnipresent and it was almost everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, you describe five trips that you took into Knin in your statement during -- that spanned much of the day. Was the level of shelling or intensity of shelling during the course of the day as you observed and experienced it constant? Did it vary? Can you describe it for us, please?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: It was not constant. The only way I can describe it was initially, the first, I would say first two, two and a half hours, was very intense. There was periods, there was periods of lull where there was no fire. There was periods where it intensified. There was various areas where the shelling was focused on and then it shifted to other areas. But to answer your question, the shelling was not intense throughout the entire period of the day. There was periods where it was not and there was periods when it was. But I would say the predominance of the intensity was the early hours of the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you indicated, you travelled to various parts of Knin to retrieve UN personnel, and actually let me ask you the question that was posed by counsel a few moments ago. What was the purpose of going into town to locate the UN personnel and did you consider it or not to be rescuing those people?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: As I indicated earlier, my responsibility was to look after the safety and security of UN personnel and we have various colour codings and I was informed about 4.00 in the morning that we've moved from code orange to code red and that indicates only one thing, that indicates that we will be launching a -- we will be regrouping the staff members at the UN headquarters. I think the first intention for us was not necessarily to rescue UN staff members, because we didn't really understand what the -- what the extent of the attack was going to be, but we certainly -- our intention was to relocate the staff members back to the UN compound. I would say that changed at 5.00 from becoming a relocation to certainly changing into a rescue mission, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, during the course of the day as you travelled to the various locations in town where UN personnel and staff members were housed, and found those people, can you describe for the Court, please, the condition or emotional state in which you found those people?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Initially, the first couple of people we located before 5.00 was concerned, but they were not -- nor were we, at that point, very concerned before 5.00, we were just handling it as a regular relocation. After 5.00, obviously things changed dramatically and staff members -- in the initial order from us was for the staff to collect their bags and to wait for us outside their residence to make the relocation as easy as possible. At 5.00 that changed because the staff then, the shelling commenced and the staff had to move to -- inside their residence or inside the basement. On your question of in which state did I find the staff members, I found the staff members in a state of extreme shock, some of them had never experienced this before, and at certain points we had to get physical with the staff members in order for them -- to convince them that leaving their homes and getting into the armoured vehicles was the right thing to do. They were totally petrified to even step outside their homes. At various occasions we had to carry them. At various occasions, we had to slap them to snap out of it and to actually walk with us or to move to the vehicles and to get into the vehicles for us to drive them back to the compound. Obviously my intention was to get all the UN staff back at the compound as safe as sound as possible and as quickly as possible to get them out of the area. So to answer your question, there was certainly a great sense of shock and -- because for us, it was really -- for the UN staff, civilian staff, it was a surprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I next have called up on screen 65 ter 1928.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, in February of 1996, did you provide to the Office of the Prosecutor a marked aerial photo on which you had marked the routes of four of the five trips you took into Knin on the 4th of August, 1995 and also the areas of shelling that you experienced and witnessed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is this that document, that is 65 ter 1928 that document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: This is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now again on this document, we see the three encircled areas in the far right part of the screen. Is it correct that as in the appendix to your February 2008 statement that we viewed a few moments ago, that those areas did not represent areas where you personally experienced or observed shelling on the 4th of August, 1995, but were aware of shelling in the ways you described earlier?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And similarly, the marking that's a bit triangular adjacent to the UN compound, is that the area where you observed the incident where the mortar and the people killed by corrected fire that was referred to in paragraph 19 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me also direct your attention, please, to two markings on this map, and the first is at the top portion, there is a thin square at the top portion of the UN compound. If that can be enlarged. That's slightly to the left of the middle of the screen as you see it. And to the immediate right of that is another square that overlays or that is interspersed with the oblong encircled area. Do you recall whether or not you made those markings on 65 ter 1928?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: I did not make them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Apart from those markings, Mr. Dreyer, are the other markings on 65 ter 1928 yours?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And as in the document we saw before, do the encircled areas represent areas in which you personally experienced or observed shelling during your trips outside the compound on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Personally observed, seen, or saw signs of shelling, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And those signs of shelling would be what?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: Impacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And although a bit difficult to see on the screen at the moment, do the coloured lines with arrow indicators accurately depict the routes of the first four of the five trips you took on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: They do as accurately as the map allowed me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Do I understand that to mean that when they enter into residential areas and move through houses, that that might not be the precise left turn or right turn you took at that time?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: That does, yeah, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we have a number for this and may it be moved into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit P79.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P79 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Registrar, if we could zoom in to -- enlarge the map slightly, perhaps, in the central area of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dreyer on the map, in addition to the circled areas, there are dots both within and outside the encircled areas. For example, the dots inside the encircled areas are easy to see. Those outside, for example, can be found toward the top of the enlarged area now or near where the cursor is now and in other locations I think the Court has identified those. Can you tell us what those dots represent, please?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER
utterances.text: The dots represent specific impact areas which I observed and as I could have managed to find them on the satellite map but those were specific impact areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour -- oh, I'm sorry. I'm just mindful of the time and this is as good a moment as any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is a good moment to stop. Mr. Dreyer, we are finished for the day. I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, not the testimony already given, not testimony still to be given, with anyone. And we'd like to see you back tomorrow, 9.00 in the morning, same courtroom. We stand adjourned until 9.00 tomorrow morning.
